title: The Help Desk - S01E01 (example notes)
audience: Fluent in English, didn't grow up in the UK
scope: An invented sample scene, written for this repository. Dialogue notes attach to quoted lines; visual notes carry a video time.

notes.text: Sample notes for an invented scene. Each note appears just after its line. “(less sure)” means: check me.
To “take the mickey” (or “take the mick”) is to tease or make fun of someone. Mildly cheeky, never harsh.
The deadpan is the joke: Pip admits the “fix” is half genuine, half a wind-up. Understatement is a staple of British comedy.
A custard cream is a classic British biscuit (a cookie, to Americans): two vanilla biscuits sandwiching a sweet cream filling.
In IT support, “P1” is the highest urgency, normally reserved for outages. Treating missing biscuits as one is the gag.
“Gutted” means bitterly disappointed. It's casual and often exaggerated for comic effect, as here.
A fiver is a five-pound note; a tenner is ten pounds. Both are everyday slang.
A “butty” is a sandwich, mostly in the North of England. A bacon butty is a bread roll with bacon, often with ketchup or brown sauce.
Putting the kettle on for tea is the British answer to nearly every situation, good or bad.
Notes about what is on screen carry a video time instead of a quote. This is where one would describe a prop or a sight gag.
